record.what_it_does: Higgsfield is a generative-media platform whose asynchronous REST API lets developers submit prompts to 40+ image, video, audio, and 3D AI models and poll or receive webhooks for the results.
record.auth_notes: Core REST API uses a key+secret pair sent as `Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` (legacy `hf-api-key`/`hf-secret` headers also still accepted). There is no OAuth2 for third-party API access to the REST API itself; the separate hosted MCP server instead authenticates end users via their Higgsfield account login (described as 'no API keys to manage'), which is a different integration layer from the documented REST API credentials.
record.access_notes: Anyone can create an account at cloud.higgsfield.ai and generate API key/secret credentials immediately at no cost, but the API is billed via account credits and the help center states generation without a paid plan is limited to a small set of models 'and doesn't include credits' — so functional use of the API requires a paid plan/credit purchase rather than being usable for free.
record.main_blocker: Real usage requires purchased credits/paid plan per account, and multi-user toolkits must manage a separate API key+secret per user (no third-party OAuth2 flow for the REST API)

evidence.quote: Send both values in the `Authorization` header: Authorization: Key YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET

Higgsfield provides one integration point for generative media models. Submit a request to a model endpoint, then poll for the result or receive a webhook when processing finishes.

record.open_questions: Exact total count of model-specific generation endpoints (docs describe 30-40+ models, each its own POST endpoint, plus shared status/cancel/estimate operations) was not fully enumerated from the OpenAPI spec due to its size; whether any free trial credit grant exists for new API accounts (a third-party blog mentioned an unofficial 1-day trial) is unconfirmed against primary docs.
